subject: Reserved pool pricing — glossary of credits, throughput and SLA redlines
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@shoreline.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@shoreline.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify 'capacity credits' vs 'GPU-hours' + SLA ladder question

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The team is close on PO approval but our finance and procurement leads asked for a few clarifications on the Dedicated pricing exhibit before we move to signatures:

1) Your pricing sheet lists "capacity credits" (CCU) and also shows a line item for "GPU-hours" — can you confirm whether CCUs are a billing abstraction (i.e., convertible to GPU-hours at variable ratios) or strictly an accounting unit tied to a pool configuration? We need precise definitions for our internal auditors.

2) The SLA remedy ladder shows service credits as a percent of monthly committed spend down to 90% availability; procurement wants to know whether partial credits can be applied per-availability-window or only at calendar-month granularity.

3) If Shoreline scales a reserved pool mid-term (adds GPUs in month 6), how do you amortize the commit and discounts? Is there proration or an up-front consumption of remaining credits?

Could you send a short one-pager or annotated redline we can circulate internally? If it's easier, happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Best,
Emily
Procurement & Ops
Shoreline AI

[Attachment: Shoreline_PO_Checklist.pdf]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@shoreline.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify 'capacity credits' vs 'GPU-hours' + SLA ladder question

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an annotated glossary and a first-pass redline addressing each point; I attached the PDF and a working doc. Short answers up front:

- Capacity Credits (CCU): an accounting unit tied to reserved pool configuration. 1 CCU maps to a defined throughput profile (e.g., 1 x A100-80GB-equivalent slot at baseline batch/seq settings) and is used for discount/commit math.
- GPU-hours: an observable usage measure (actual GPU compute time consumed). We report both; billing uses CCUs for reservation amortization and GPU-hours for overage reconciliation.
- SLA credits: we can offer windowed credits (per 24-hour rolling window) or monthly aggregation — by default we apply at month level but can accept per-window credits if Shoreline requires it for audit reasons.
- Mid-term scaling: we propose an amortization schedule (attached) that prorates remaining commit over the contract term and applies new CCUs at the sub-tier discount for the remainder.

I'll loop in Laura and Dev to confirm the legal-redline language. If you want a short call, we can do 10–2 PT tomorrow.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserved_pricing_glossary_v2.pdf]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>; Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed redlines for Shoreline — definitions + remedies

Team —

Read Sergio's draft. Notes for negotiation and legal: please keep comments inline in the .docx but a few strategic points below.

1) Definitions: avoid variable language like "equivalent slot" — replace with deterministic mapping table (model family -> CCU multiplier -> baseline tokens/sec). This prevents future disputes when customers change model mix.

2) Billing: insist on CCU-based reserved amortization with GPU-hours only for overages. If they insist on GPU-hour accounting inside the reservation, we must tighten measurement windows and sampling methodology.

3) SLA remedies: accept per-24hr window credits as a concession, but cap aggregate credits to 30% of monthly commit unless legal approves higher. Also add a clause allowing Redwood to execute failover traffic to compatible model variants during exceptional outages without breaching SLA (keeps services online).

4) Mid-term scaling: propose a "scale-attach" flow where additional CCUs are priced at the then-current list price but discounts are blended using a time-weighted average across the remaining term; include an example calculation in the schedule.

5) Early termination: procurement may ask for an exit amortization refund. Suggest offering pro-rated refund minus a 3-month non-refundable commit (protects capacity planning).

I attached a proposed redline (proposed_redlines_SH-2027-042.docx) and an amortization schedule. Please add comments by EOD tomorrow; we'll consolidate and send to Emily.

- Laura
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_redlines_SH-2027-042.docx]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: proposed redlines for Shoreline — definitions + remedies

Laura / team —

Quick technical clarifications to include in the glossary so procurement can't claim ambiguity later:

- "Baseline throughput" should be defined as tokens-per-second measured over a 5-minute sustained window using Redwood's benchmark harness (model/version/seq-length specified). We should include the exact benchmark commit id in the contract.

- "KV/prefix cache" credits: some workloads get outsized benefit from caching. Add an explicit statement that CCU consumption is measured on decoded tokens after cache application; provide example math showing how caching reduces GPU-hours but not CCU amortization.

- "Burst capacity": define burst as short-lived capacity above baseline with a defined bucket size (e.g., 3000 GPU-seconds) and a replenishment cadence. Make sure burst usage is billed as GPU-hours, not drawn from CCU amortization.

I'll update the glossary PDF to include these measurement conventions.

- Dev
Principal Systems Engineer, Inference Runtime

[Attachment: capacity_amortization_schedule.xlsx]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@shoreline.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@shoreline.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify 'capacity credits' vs 'GPU-hours' + SLA ladder question

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Attached are three items: 1) an annotated glossary that maps CCUs to a deterministic hardware/throughput table; 2) a redline with the proposed SLA remedy ladder and per-window credit option; 3) an amortization schedule showing blended discounts for mid-term scaling.

Key takeaways (short):
- CCUs are a reservation/accounting construct; they determine discount tiering and reserved billing amortization.
- Actual consumption is tracked in GPU-hours; overages are billed at the agreed overage rate and do not change reservation discounts retroactively.
- We can accept per-24hr window credits but recommend capping aggregate credits to 30% of monthly committed spend; language in the redline explains enforcement and measurement windows.
- Scaling mid-term: new CCUs are assigned the then-current list price and discounts are blended using the attached schedule; we included an example where Shoreline grows 40% in month 6.

Next steps: review the attachments and let us know if procurement wants the per-window credit option enabled. If yes, we'll update the term sheet and prepare DocuSign. We can also run a quick 20-min call to walk through the amortization example.

Best regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
